newsitem.title: UK: Rank makes disposals and sees charges.
newsitem.headline: Rank makes disposals and sees charges.

text.p: British leisure firm Rank Group Plc said on Thursday it had disposed of peripheral businesses worth over 200 million pounds ($333.2 million) since the half year and said it expected to take restructuring charges.
The company also said it sold coach holiday operator Shearings to a new firm formed by NatWest Ventures Ltd and Shearings' management team for 83 million pounds.
Rank said it would use the proceeds to cut debt.
The company said its provision for its previously-announced restructuring plans in 1996 would be about 35 million pounds, most of which would be spent next year.

At the year end, the company's property revaluation reserve stood at 186 million pounds at year-end 1995. A reduction in the valuation as a result of accounting changes, will result in a charge of about 150 million pounds.
Of that amount, about two-thirds was related to Rank's bingo and UK holiday operations.
Rank said both the property charge and the restructuring cost would be charged to operating profit at the year end.
Rank said it expected non-operating items to include a net loss on disposals of about 50 million pounds, mainly historic goodwill previously written-off to reserves.
The company said it expected investment expenditure for the year to December 31 to total some 900 million pounds compared to 366 million pounds last year.
This year's total will include capital spending of about 485 million pounds and acquisitions of 415 million pounds.

Regarding Rank Xerox, the firm's venture with US firm Xerox Corp, the company said a payment of 40 million pounds net would be received before year-end 1996, compared to 53 million pounds net for 1995.
The company, reiterating that it does not plan to keep its interest in Rank Xerox in the long-term, said part of the reduction was due to its reduced stake in the venture.
Rank's shares were marked down 9.5p at 432.5 by 0842 GMT.
Besides Shearings, Rank said it sold Kingston Plantation for about 30 million pounds, its inland amusement arcade business for 25 million pounds, and Precision Industries for 72 million pounds.
At November 30, the company had net debt of about 1.0 billion pounds, with just over half held in dollars and most of the rest in pounds. ($1=.6003 Pound)
